oneLine: Tax on the profit you make when you sell something for more than it cost.
explanation: A capital asset is almost anything you own for personal use or to invest, such as a home or stocks. When you sell one, the difference between its cost and the sale price is a capital gain or a capital loss.
You have a capital gain if you sell for more than the asset cost you. You have a capital loss if you sell for less.
A gain is long-term if you held the asset for more than one year. It is short-term if you held it for one year or less.
whyItMatters: How long you hold an investment can change the tax on its profit. Long-term gains often have a lower tax rate than short-term gains. Losses can lower your tax too, but losses on personal things, such as your home or car, do not count.
workedExample: You buy shares for $1,000 and sell them two years later for $1,500. Your capital gain is $500, and it is long-term. At a 15% rate, the tax on it is $75.

inTheUs.text: Short-term gains are taxed like your other income. Long-term gains are taxed at 0%, 15% or 20%, depending on your taxable income. For a single person in 2025, the 0% rate applies up to $48,350. Up to $3,000 of net losses a year can lower your other income.
